headline: Learned representations of proteins, cells and compounds from spatial and imaging data
label: Attention Based Biomolecular Prediction
summary: Transformer, graph-attention, contrastive and variational models are now trained on millions of cells to produce representations that transfer across platforms…
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned representation models built on attention, transformer, graph-attention, contrastive or variational architectures and applied to large single-cell, spatial and microscopy data. Spatium trains a protein language foundation model on over 51 million cells across spatial proteomics platforms, targeting panel-robust cell representations, and SpatialFormer, a hybrid CNN-transformer, is pretrained on 17M Xenium-profiled cells for niche-aware representations used in batch correction and annotation. UDIST and MICON address unsupervised or contrastive phenotypic profiling in 2D microscopy, with MICON modelling chemical compounds as treatments. The hierarchical graph attention autoencoder models dose-specific single-cell olaparib resistance, and the deep mechanistic model couples semi-supervised representation learning with an ODE model of EGFR/MAPK signalling. What is new is the coupling of representation learning with explicit dose-resolved or mechanistic structure. The items do not benchmark these architectures against one another.
